reason: Refuted as specified. One part survives, and it is not this idea's own. (1) Replacing exp52 by the no-insertion twin {ILM, LM} holds up on private: the twin wins in 14 of 15 MC scenarios (dU +0.006..+0.22). exp52 shares the insertion and the V1284 head with F1, so it fails in the same worlds. But that part is idea noins-twin-f2. v3 section f already has a variant-F2 clause (public F1 >= 0.954, L34 <= 7.5 h, honest gate, variant >= F1 - 0.001, forks differ), and R4 already makes a D scored at 0/+0.001 an F2 candidate. So the calculator's case (1) is mostly v3 behaviour, and most of the claimed +0.02..+0.08 P(medal) is double-counted. (2) What is distinctive here does not survive transfer-realistic assumptions: rule (1), {stack, stack+variance rider} whenever D is scored, and choosing by a committed MC with a lab-calibrated table. The metric is adj_edge_J + 0.1*div_J with div_J ~0.36. Public is ~29% of <= ~100 embryo-disjoint clips, so about 22 public GT divisions. There one net division TP is worth ~+0.0025 and one FP ~-0.0013. The insertion's '+0.001 twice' is therefore about one division event, measured twice on the SAME public clips (#28/#27 and #35/#34), not two replicates. A realistic private I is ~N(+0.0005, 0.001-0.0015), not N(+0.0008, 0.0008). Under that I, P(>X), which decides medal vs no medal, is 0.926/0.923 for the twin and only 0.910/0.854 for the D-pair even with D's private mean at +0.0005. It falls to 0.889/0.827 at mean 0 and 0.871/0.805 at mean -0.0005. Even under the lens's own I, the D-pair only ties the twin at D mean 0 (0.949 vs 0.950) and loses at -0.0005 (0.939) or with corr 0.5 between I and D (0.930). Both are fork-only riders on the same few private divisions. The D-pair wins only on silver, and only when I is confidently positive. U weights bronze and silver equally, which pushes it toward variance exactly where the medal cliff favours the twin. (3) The calibration step imports in-sample artefacts. |delta_44b6 - delta_6bba| from the exp60 lab is in-sample for DaughterNet, the edge net and the head (edge filter: +0.016 local, 0 on LB). For DeepCenter, trained on 44b6 only, it measures in-sample bias, not private noise. '0.5 x public delta' at 3 decimals is quantisation (0 or +0.0005). Where the MC could differ from the simple rule (exp52's sd, I's private sd), its inputs cannot be calibrated. Where they can, it equals the simple rule. Not a node-count artefact (I and D leave nodes unchanged, and lowrefine is shared) and not a closed line. The flaw is the rule and the false precision. Scripts: session scratchpad pair_skeptic_mc.py, _mc2.py, _mc3.py; numbers in research/wf_ideas_v4/v_private-finals_finals-pair-calculator_value.notes.md.
fix: Drop the calculator and its lab calibration. Pre-register a fixed rule in CONTEXT.md section f before 27 Sep 12:00 UTC. (a) F1 = the fullest R3/R4-admissible x138-family stack with C01, as in v3. (b) F2 = the stack with NO fork riders (the no-insertion twin exp58n/exp59n = K2/K3 minus divinsert, plus minus any DeepCenter threshold), if it is scored, error-free, R5-admissible and public >= 0.953. The insertion and D are both fork-only riders measured on about 22 public divisions, so the medal-cliff hedge is to leave all of them out of F2 together. {ILMD, LM} gives P(>X) 0.92-0.95, about equal to {ILM, LM}, in every scenario. (c) A D scored at 0/+0.001 (R4 F2 candidate) should NOT displace the twin as F2. It goes into F1 only by R4 (+0.002). (d) exp52 only if no twin is scored (branch D or S3/S9 not used). (e) Keep the other constraints: never exp56, never byte-identical files, manual ticking, and print the submission IDs. The objective is P(private > X) first: note that the bronze line may sit above X if more than ~390 teams end above x138 (rank-arithmetic-watch). The MC can stay in the notes as rationale, not as the decider. Effort ~0.2 h (a CONTEXT edit), and the value depends on the noins-twin-f2 slot being used.
realistic_gain: 0 on public. This idea's own increment over 'v3 section f + noins-twin-f2' is <= 0 in transfer-realistic worlds: its rule (1) would lose 0.016-0.13 P(>X) against the twin when the insertion's private sd is >= 0.001. It is positive (~+0.01 P(>X), +0.04-0.07 P(silver)) only if the insertion is confidently positive on private and D's private mean is >= +0.0005. The robust gain, about +0.02 to +0.1 P(>X) vs exp52, belongs to the twin (noins-twin-f2) and to the fixed 'F2 = no-fork-rider twin' rule.
